assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: His history belongs to him at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: the promise with Mika, the artificial heart and his meeting with the child about ten years before the present (E09 flashback), and a first meeting with Mika earlier still (E07). Located present states: the regular who commissioned Walnut's breach and believes the problem cleaned up (E01-E02); the conversation with Mika about the rule against involvement (E04); the E05 test arranged from his side; the claim on Chisato, Takina's report and Mika's plea (E07); Himegama's intervention (E08); Majima's threat (E10); the researcher's recordings (E11); the confrontation, the ultimatum and Chisato's shot (E12); and the last meeting with Mika, the window and the reported death with the card (E13). Two capability states are split at E12, when Chisato tells him her own account of her happiness. Nothing after E13; print stories are outside scope.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: 'Predictable choices and where to abstain' gives a discriminating account. Yoshimatsu's fixed criterion is that a person's talent is a gift from God whose realization is that person's role and happiness (E08 to Himegama, E07 to Mika, E12 to Chisato). His instruments change with the relationship and with each failure ('Failure changes his instruments faster than his criterion'). With an adult he likes and needs, such as Mika, he appeals to their personal promise (E04, E07, E09). With a subordinate he combines praise, a constrained choice and an expectation that she can do it (E08 Himegama). With Robota he gives polite applause to a tool (E02). With a beneficiary who wants another life he reads her wishes through what he thinks her talent means (E07 Takina, E12 Chisato). When affection and the criterion conflict, the criterion decides: he calls Chisato a dying doll he did not wind for helping people, and says doing it for her and for the world are the same thing (E12). The model predicts his mistakes: he believes Walnut has been disposed of while Walnut sits in the same cafe (E02), turns Takina's report of Chisato's attachment into an expectation of service (E07), and accepts blame for failed execution while leaving almost no room to be wrong about what Chisato owed (E10). Not A: the portrait says it cannot tell what would persuade him to take a recipient's testimony as decisive, or which threat he would choose in a wholly new case, and his E04 motive for returning stays unsettled. Not C: the deciding priority is shown, not only the acts. What stays open is the exact instrument, which is productive uncertainty within this scope.

Located states: the promise and the surgery about ten years before the present (E09 flashback); the warm regular who is pleased to be remembered (E01-E02); the E04 conversation with Mika about the rule against involvement; the claim on Chisato and the plea Mika makes in vain (E07); the escalation through agents (E05 test, E06, E08 harm, E10 Majima, E11 the researcher); the E12 ultimatum, after which Chisato shoots him to protect Takina; and the E13 meeting where he says he was not understood and seems no longer needed, before his reported death. Not B: the escalation is partly indirect, since the portrait does not establish a single remote operator in E05 or his understanding of the E08 clinical plan, and the decade between the promise and E01 is unshown. His E13 hurt carries no recantation, so no transition of his criterion is located. Not D: each state is placed by episode and timecode, and the portrait states that the criterion persists while the instruments change.

Located lexicon and addressee contrasts: 掃除 for the work that put him at the cafe (E02); talent as God's gift, the role indicated at birth and a clear role as happiness (E08, E12); 'we promised' and 'our daughter' to Mika (E07, E09); たきなちゃん to Takina (E07); polite applause and 'tool-like' for Robota (E02); 救世主 with the child (E09); 'we only helped' to the researcher (E11); 'a dying doll' (E12); and the contrast between his corporate 'we' and the first-person lines of E13, where the Japanese subtitles write 私 and two attributed listener reports hear あたし. Not B: the portrait gives no register rules, and it says the disputed E13 readings settle neither an invariant pronunciation nor a personal category. Not D: the recurring lexicon and the contrast in address are located with named listeners.

Located cafe comforts only: being pleased that Chisato remembers him, a souvenir from Russia and putting off her question about Mika (E02); liking Mika's ohagi and recalling when Mika could hardly brew coffee (E02); praising Himegama's cooking (E08). The portrait calls these small comforts in a private life the show gives sparingly, and says his ordinary life away from family, work and the cafe is unknown. Not C: the instances are few and confined to the cafe and one meal. Not E: they recur across visits and are located.

Directed differences: Mika (an intimate history in the two men's own terms, 'our daughter', the promise, 'liar' and hurt in E13); Chisato (the giver she recognizes, the role he claims for her, the ultimatum, her refusal and his reply); Takina (たきなちゃん, an attachment read as service, the prediction that she cannot shoot him in front of Chisato in E12); Himegama (praise with a constrained choice); Robota (asymmetric applause); Majima (praise as an outstanding Alan Child and his own life offered as a resource, E10); the heart researcher (credit for his skill, no authority over the patient, E11). Not A: the relationship with Mika is unnamed, the portrait abstains on its status, and his life before Mika is untested. Not C: each relationship has located states and a stated difference in how he treats the person.

Self-statements are few and located: wanting to see Mika (E04, whose motive the portrait does not settle); his heart leaping at the cafe as on the day they met (E07); calling Chisato's departure from her path his own mistake (E10); not being understood and seeming no longer needed (E13); and the card read in his attributed voice (E13). The portrait says he is more readable in dialogue than in interiors. Not C: there is no inner monologue, and the portrait declines to assign his visits to a single motive. Not E: the stated feelings are located against his acts.

Located modes with outcomes: putting off a question with warmth (E02); invoking a rule, then asking whether he is being told to disappear and returning to the promise (E04); 'we promised' against Mika's plea, met by Mika's threat (E07); interrupting Takina (E07); answering Majima's threat with praise and the offer of his own life (E10); urging the researcher to think of future patients and entrust the subject to him (E11); asserting his purpose over Chisato's testimony, offering his own death, then using Takina's danger to renew the demand (E12); calling Mika a liar and showing the returned pendant (E13). The portrait states the pattern: the pressure grows more violent as he tries to make his prediction come true. Not A: the portrait says which threat he would choose in a wholly new case exceeds the source, and several escalations run through agents with purposes of their own. Not C: the modes and the escalation are located across many episodes.

His principle is stated and applied: talent belongs to God, not to its bearer or supporters (E07); one girl's life is a small cost if a man's talent bears fruit, and future patients justify control of the present one (E11); his own life is a resource for the ideal (E10, E12); he accepts blame for execution but not for the criterion (E10). Not B: he asserts rather than weighs; no scene shows him weighing alternatives or changing a choice on a moral ground, and the portrait cannot say what would make a recipient's testimony decisive. Not D: the principle and its applications are located across E07-E12.

Few located instances: laughing and deferring Chisato's question about Mika (E02); the remark about returning to see Mika, which Mika calls teasing (E04); laughing and thanking the child when she says he is lying about working at the hospital (E09). The portrait reads the first as making a social situation pleasurable for someone who matters to him. Not C: there is no account of when or how he plays beyond these scenes. Not E: the instances are located and one function is described.

One dedicated portrait covers E01-E13 with timecodes, cue numbers and claim, behaviour and relationship IDs, and separates the attributed print comparisons from the continuity. Not A: the row curates only this derived item; the ledgers and readings behind it are not on the row; and several facts the model touches stay open in the source (the E05 operator, the E08 clinical plan, who receives the device, whether the heart is in his chest, the physical cause of his death). Not C: every major appearance and decision is located.

Located bounds against overreading: the name Alan Adams is not his legal identity, and his rank, jurisdiction and training are not enumerated; his E04 motive is not settled; the portrait abstains on the legal status, sexual history and domestic schedule of his relationship with Mika; no single remote operator is established in E05; the E08 clinical plan and his understanding of its consequences are open; E11 does not establish who receives the device; his claim that the heart is in his chest is unverified; the contact and severity of Chisato's shot are open; the E13 pronoun readings are disputed; the cause, retrieval and consent of his reported death are unresolved, and Chisato's acceptance of his last interpretation is unshown; no recantation is given in E13; the child did not need a script to read the gift as a gun for saving people; and the print panels are not his own expectations. Not A: no forecast about him is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

States are placed by episode and timecode, and the promise is placed about ten years before the present. Not B: there is no story calendar, and the decade between the promise and E01 is unshown. Not D: the episode states are precisely located.

conditions: Illustrative lines only, with Mika, Chisato, Takina, Himegama, Robota or Majima, built from the located lexicon and address (E02, E04, E07-E13).
Warm cafe small talk that defers a private question (E02), or a reminder of a personal promise to Mika (E07).
Excluded: an invariant first-person pronoun or pronunciation, new threat wording, and his last card treated as a pattern for other speech.
scenario_readiness.note: The discovery row claims speech. The located lexicon of talent, role, happiness, promise and savior, and the contrasts in address, constrain illustrative lines in the sampled relationships. Exact pronunciation and the E13 pronoun are not established.

conditions: A person shows a capacity he values: predict that he names it and speaks to the worth of realizing it, as with Himegama's cooking and Chisato's talent (E08, E12).
A person he likes chooses against his purpose: predict that his language tightens around the capacity he named and that he reads her wishes through it (E07, E12).
A known adult whose cooperation he needs: predict an appeal to a personal promise before a simple threat (E04, E07).
A subordinate: predict praise, a constrained choice and an expectation that she can do it (E08).
A threat to his life: predict that he treats his own death as a resource for the purpose (E10, E12).

A beneficiary's testimony about her own happiness: predict that he asserts his purpose as prior to her judgment (E12). After E12, predict hurt and a sense of being unneeded, with no recantation (E13).
Include his mistakes: misreading outcomes he cannot see, turning attachment into expected service, and accepting blame for execution rather than for the criterion.
Separate, lower-confidence condition: a comparable new beneficiary or agent, transferred from the sampled cases.

Exclude which threat he would choose in a wholly new case, what would persuade him, a recipient who declines a gift freely, money promised to someone without exceptional talent, his family obligations before meeting Mika, and any generalization of his final act into a policy.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Television E01-E13. His promise with Mika, the surgery and his meeting with the child belong to him at every state. Two capability states are used: before E12, when Chisato has refused the role but has not yet told him her account of her happiness; and E12-E13, after her testimony, her shot and the returned pendant. Nothing after his reported death in E13.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Mika as the adult partner in the promise; Chisato as the beneficiary; Takina as Chisato's partner; Himegama, Robota and Majima as agents or accomplices; the heart researcher as a professional whose skill he needs. A comparable new beneficiary or agent is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: Cafe LycoReco, the Alan Institute's operations as the series shows them, and the E12-E13 confrontation settings.
No print scene, no account of his Alan rank or private training, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded extrapolation follows the portrait's conditional rules. The criterion is predicted; the instrument he picks in a new case is not.

conditions: Visits to Cafe LycoReco and meals with people he likes: pleasure at being remembered, souvenirs, food and old jokes, keeping a history private without withdrawing warmth (E02, E04, E07, E08).
His home, family and life away from the cafe and his work are not modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Only cafe visits and one meal are located.

conditions: Predict that he defends a choice by the talent principle: talent belongs to God, a clear role is happiness, and a present life may be spent for a talent's fruition or for future beneficiaries (E07, E08, E11, E12).
Predict that he accepts blame for a failed execution, not for the criterion (E10).
Excluded: genuine weighing of alternatives, a change of mind on a moral ground, and what argument would move him.
scenario_readiness.note: His principle and its applications are located; he is never shown weighing alternatives.

The portrait supports an intimate history with Mika in the two men's own terms and abstains on any name for it, its legal status, sexual history or domestic arrangements. A romance scenario would rest on invention.

conditions: Commissioning and paying for work, and directing agents with praise, a constrained choice and an expectation (E01, E06, E08).
Dealing with a professional whose skill he needs: credit for the skill, an appeal to future beneficiaries and control of the subject (E11).
Excluded: his Alan rank, succession, jurisdiction and training; the exact operational and clinical plans carried out by others; and his authority over the device's recipient.

known_limits.statement: The portrait leaves considerable room for not knowing what would persuade him to take a recipient's testimony as decisive.
The portrait says that extrapolating which threat he would select in a wholly new case would exceed what the source gives.
Several escalations run through agents with purposes of their own: no single remote operator is established in E05, and the E08 clinical plan and his understanding of its consequences remain open.
The name Alan Adams is not supplied as his legal identity, and his rank, succession rights, jurisdiction, family origin and training are not enumerated.
The intimate history with Mika is supported in the two men's own terms; the portrait abstains on its legal status, sexual history and shared domestic schedule.
His claim that the heart is in his own chest is unverified, and E11 does not establish who receives the device.

The physical cause, retrieval and consensual basis of his reported death are unresolved, and Chisato's acceptance of his final interpretation is unshown. The terminal act is not generalized into a policy.
The Japanese subtitles write 私 in his E13 lines and two attributed listener reports hear あたし; neither an invariant pronunciation nor a personal category is established.
The Reload, Reload 02, Repeat and Recollect scenes are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity and are not used for prediction.
Untested: a recipient who declines a gift freely, money promised to someone without exceptional talent, his family obligations before meeting Mika, and the terms of later consent after the tower.
His ordinary life away from family, work and the cafe is not shown.
